To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the retrieval of aerosol profiles from UV/VIS observations using a small number (3 or 4) of parameters is possible, but requires a regularisation and a dynamic choice of parameters of the regulariser, and that a retrieval sequence based on the information content of previous measurements and additional intensities can improve the solution significantly.
the retrieval of aerosol profiles from UV/VIS measurements can be performed by using a Tikhonova regularisation with an L-curve criterion.
the retrieval of aerosol optical properties in a boundary layer from MAX-DOAs observations requires regularisation and that the choice of the regularising parameter is crucial for a good solution.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regularised least-squares approach for aerosol extinction profile retrieval from MAX-DOAs measurements is a powerful tool for boundary layer reconstruction, if a dynamic choice of regularisation parameters is made, and that it is important to use all available information in the retrieval sequence to improve the quality of the solution.

a regularised least-squares retrieval can be used to reconstruct the aerosol extinction profile in the boundary layer from MAX-DOAs observations with a good precision and accuracy, provided that the retrieval is performed in a dynamic and adaptive way.

the retrieval of aerosol extinctions in the boundary layer using MAX-DOAS measurements is feasible and can be improved by regularisation, the use of a sequence of observations, and by using intensities in the retrieval.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a retrieval approach for a boundary layer aerosol profile parameterisation can be designed in a way that is flexible with respect to different measurement geometries and aerosol load.

the inversion of a pure least-squares retrieval problem for a boundary layer aerosol profile requires regularisation, that a priori information can be used to improve the retrieval, and that the information content of a measurement series can be used to optimise the a priori information.
a pure least-squares inversion of the radiance equation for a boundary layer profile is feasible if the regularisation is adapted dynamically and if a retrieval sequence is used for the retrieval.
